transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Start time: 09:30 PST
Duration: ~1h12m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood), Diego Ramos (Redwood), Maya Patel (Haven), Tom Rivera (Haven), Elena Voss (Haven)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- High level: Implementation intake to scope pilot for Haven Digital's generative search assistant.
- Key asks: VPC/private deployment option, KMS/HSM support, SLAs, and initial perf targets.

[00:00] Avery Chen: okay good morning everyone, thanks for making time, uh this is Avery at Redwood, i'll kick us off real quick, um goal today is to align on scope and next steps for the onboarding pilot for Haven Digital.
[00:12] Speaker 2 (Diego): hi all, Diego here, i'll be owning the customer success side and the runbook, and i'll coordinate the checkpoints.
[00:20] Maya Patel: thanks, appreciate it. quick background — we're standing up an internal generative search assistant that serves product docs and private customer data, so security and residency are huge for us.
[00:30] Tom Rivera: and from infra side we need clarity on networking — whether we do Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, or full Private VPC. also curious about cost delta and latency tradeoffs.
[00:42] Elena Voss: hello, i'm Elena. we'll need SOC2 scope evidence, audit logs for queries, and KMS integration for keys. we also have a requirement for SSO and SCIM for admin access.
[00:55] Avery Chen: perfect, that's aligned. quick agenda — 1) success criteria and timeline, 2) deployment options and security, 3) pilot size and perf benchmarks, 4) next steps. if anything to add raise your hand.

[01:15] Maya: sounds good. i can walk through our timeline — we want a pilot in january, production by march, assuming pilot hits X. by pilot we mean about 100k monthly tokens across a small set of endpoints and up to 200 qps peak burst for internal alpha users.
[01:34] Avery: good baseline. would you consider a smaller pilot first just to validate integration? sometimes customers do a two-week smoke test with synthetic traffic to validate routing and SLOs.
[01:44] Tom: yes we can do that. the big ask is that we mimic our real traffic distribution — sequence lengths vary, some long-document context. also, we rely heavily on prefix caching and want to understand KV cache behaviour.
[01:58] Diego: note, Redwood's platform has automatic prefix/KV caching options but we'll need to set TTLs to match your data cadence — we'll include config suggestions in the runbook. (mumbled)

[02:15] Elena: on security — does Redwood support customer-managed keys? we can't have our keys in vendor-managed KMS.
[02:22] Avery: yes, for Private deployments we support BYOK via customer KMS, including HSM-backed key rotation policies. for Dedicated we have KMS integrations; i'll send the specifics.
[02:34] Elena: are audit logs immutable and exportable to our SIEM?
[02:38] Avery: yes, audit logs can be streamed to customer S3 or a SIEM via syslog with per-request metadata. small caveat — some metadata names in the console are abbreviated in the UI, apologies if the naming's confusing when you look at the docs.
[02:52] Maya: good. about data residency — unfortunately we need EU data to stay in eu-west-1. can Redwood route production traffic regionally?
[03:02] Avery: yes, regional routing is supported. requests can be pinned by policy and we can set region-specific model variants. for the pilot you can choose a region-matched endpoint.

[03:18] Tom: curious about fallback/ graceful degradation — if the dedicated pool hits capacity, what's the behaviour?
[03:23] Diego: we often configure automated fallback to compatible model variants or burst to hosted capacity if the policy allows it. that reduces error rates but may affect cost and slightly increase latency.
[03:35] Tom: okay, cost/latency tradeoff — do you have unit economics guidance for 8-bit quantized variants vs fp16? our model is a 13b open model.
[03:46] Avery: yes, Optimize can recommend quantization strategies. as a rough ballpark, 8-bit quantization can reduce token cost by 30–50% with modest perf tradeoffs; latency can improve on some hardware but depends on the kernel selection. we'll run bench tests in the SE deep dive.

[04:05] Elena: about compliance — we need a copy of your SOC 2 report and also controls mapping for ISO. and also legal will want a DPA with data processing terms.
[04:15] Avery: understood. i'll attach the security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, DPA template) after. Diego will provide the contact for our legal team.

[04:28] Maya: what's the expected lead time for Dedicated reserved capacity? we can't wait months.
[04:33] Diego: typically provisioning depends on config; reserved pools can be reserved in weeks with committed capacity. Dedicated can be faster if we pre-approve images and use our standard SKU set, we can aim for 3–4 weeks for a basic pool but Private VPC/on-prem can take longer.
[04:50] Tom: can we do an initial hosted pilot and then move to Dedicated once we're happy?
[04:55] Avery: yes, that's a common path — start hosted for speed, then migrate with pinned model versions and rollout policies. the API surface remains the same, so minimal app changes.

[05:07] Maya: performance benchmarks — we'd like a latency p50 of <120ms for short prompts and p95 <350ms for median-sized prompts. is that realistic?
[05:18] Avery: it's plausible for a 13b quantized model on dedicated GPUs with proper batching, but we'll need to verify with real traffic. the SE team will run a targeted benchmark.

[05:33] Tom: on network egress and VPC peering, do you support private peering to our VPC and cross-account IAM roles?
[05:40] Diego: yes, we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and IAM cross-account where applicable. there are a few setup steps — we'll include those in the infra checklist.

[05:50] Speaker 1 (Maya): any gotchas customers run into?
[05:53] Avery: timing on key rotation and plugin compatibility sometimes surprises teams. also tokenization mismatch across model variants can cause small dev regressions — we recommend pinning tokenizer and model versions in your integration tests.

[06:08] Elena: one more on logs — we want per-token cost breakdown for billing reconciliation. can Redwood provide token-level cost attribution?
[06:15] Avery: yes, the console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per token and per route. for enterprise billing we can share CSV exports and billing APIs.

[06:28] Tom: will there be any outage windows for migration?
[06:31] Diego: migrations can be done with canary rollouts and automatic fallback; planned maintenance windows are communicated in advance and SLAs apply for Dedicated.

[06:45] Maya: ok let's talk timeline concrete — we agreed to a pilot in january, with a smoke test in mid-december. action items to exchange docs and schedule the SE deep dive.
[06:58] Avery: recap — Redwood to send security pack and runbook, Haven to share traffic samples and SLOs, schedule SE deep dive week of Dec 6. any objections?
[07:10] Elena: none from security, we'll review the SOC2 pack.
[07:14] Tom: sounds good from infra.
[07:16] Maya: good, thanks.
[07:18] Diego: i'll follow up with calendar invites and the runbook link. i'll also open a pilot ticket in our CRM.

[07:28] Avery: thanks everyone, appreciate it. end of call.
